translationRepairs: In Shaotai year 2 (550), as a southern-river strongman he was made roaming-cavalry general by precedent.
In Shaotai year 2 (556), as a southern-river strongman he was made roaming-cavalry general by precedent.
Shaotai year 2 was AD 556; the parenthetical 550 is six years too early.
In Shaotai year 2, as a southern-river magnate Tanlang was by precedent made roaming-cavalry general.
In Shaotai year 2 (556), as a southern-river magnate Tanlang was by precedent made roaming-cavalry general.
Adding the correct Western equivalent makes the literal field consistent with the dated idiomatic field.
In Shaotai year 2 (550) he was made interior administrator of Linchuan.
In Shaotai year 2 (556) he was made interior administrator of Linchuan.
This second occurrence of Shaotai year 2 likewise corresponds to AD 556, not 550.

Collation variant: (Tianjia). In spring of the third year, [3] Emperor Wen pardoned southern-river people led astray by Di and ordered Jiang inspector Wu Mingche to command all forces with Gao inspector Huang Fading and Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu against Di.

In spring of Tianjia year 3 (562), Emperor Wen pardoned the southern-river people who had been misled by Di and ordered Jiangzhou inspector Wu Mingche to command all forces, together with Gaozhou inspector Huang Fading and Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu, in a campaign against Di.
The English should translate the historical sentence directly, supply the correct date, and omit collation apparatus and bracket markers from the prose.
At Poyang, Xinwu cave lord Yu Xiaoqing rose for Lin.
When Wang Lin reached Pencheng, Yu Xiaoqing, lord of the Xinwu cave settlement, raised troops in support of him.
湓城 is Pencheng near Jiujiang, distinct from Poyang (鄱陽), which appears elsewhere in the chapter.

We now send pacifying-the-south equal-in-honor's army marshal, Xiangdong duke's chancellor Liu Guangde, with pacifying-the-west marshal Sun Xiao, North Xin'ai administrator Lu Guangda, credential-bearing pacifying-the-south general and Wu inspector Marquis of Pengze Lu Xida, and ten thousand armored men, marching from Xingkou.

We now dispatch Liu Guangde, army marshal to the general who guards the south and chancellor to the Duke of Xiangdong; Sun Xiao, concurrently army marshal to the general who pacifies the west; Lu Guangda, administrator of northern Xincai; and Lu Xida, bearer of credentials, general who pacifies the south, inspector of Wuzhou, and Marquis of Pengze, with ten thousand armored men marching from Xingkou.
The proposal correctly restores Northern Xincai but leaves the office string cramped. This revision separates each appointee and office without dropping any title.
Baoying armed Di with troops and stores; Liu Yi also sent his second son, the Loyal Subject, to follow.
Baoying armed Di with troops and stores; Liu Yi also sent his second son Zhongchen to follow.
忠臣 is the son's personal name Zhongchen, not the common noun phrase 'the Loyal Subject.'
Next spring Andu smashed the palisades. Yi and his second son Chuxin fled to Chen Baoying. Several thousand followers, men and women, were taken.
Next spring Andu smashed the palisades. Yi and his second son Zhongchen fled to Chen Baoying. Several thousand followers, men and women, were taken.
The same son is named Zhongchen here; Chuxin has no basis in the characters 忠臣.

In Shaotai year 2, for aiding the court, he was made bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, trust-military general, inspector of Jingzhou with concurrent Dongyang prefect, and marquis of Yongxing county [7] with a fief of five hundred households. On [7]: the Southern History reads Yongjia.

In Shaotai year 2 (556), for aiding the court, he was made bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, general who inspires martial might, inspector of Jinzhou, and concurrently administrator of Dongyang; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing County with five hundred households.
縉州 is Jinzhou, the date is AD 556, and the collation marker and Southern History note do not belong inside the translated prose.
Collation variant: still; adopted reading: but also be promoted and rewarded.
He was also rewarded and promoted.
仍加賞擢 is ordinary narrative prose. The current output exposes collation machinery, while the proposal begins with an ungrammatical lowercase conjunction.
